problem_text:
A logistics company needs to schedule 6 delivery trucks to handle 6 different customer routes.

Each route consists of a sequence of checkpoint stops represented as pairs (Truck Type, Handling Time),
where each pair specifies the specialized truck type required for that checkpoint and the time needed to complete the handling.
The order of pairs indicates the mandatory sequence in which checkpoints must be visited.

Route details:
* Route 1 requires the sequence: (T6, 2) → (T5, 8) → (T1, 1) → (T4, 3) → (T2, 9) → (T3, 5)
* Route 2 requires the sequence: (T1, 3) → (T6, 3) → (T4, 3) → (T2, 4) → (T5, 10) → (T3, 6)
* Route 3 requires the sequence: (T1, 5) → (T4, 6) → (T5, 3) → (T6, 4) → (T3, 6) → (T2, 4)
* Route 4 requires the sequence: (T2, 10) → (T4, 1) → (T5, 3) → (T6, 10) → (T1, 1) → (T3, 7)
* Route 5 requires the sequence: (T6, 9) → (T2, 1) → (T5, 1) → (T1, 1) → (T3, 2) → (T4, 10)
* Route 6 requires the sequence: (T5, 7) → (T2, 7) → (T6, 10) → (T3, 6) → (T4, 4) → (T1, 3)

Each checkpoint handling must proceed without interruption once it begins,
and each specialized truck can only service one checkpoint at a time.
The objective is to determine the optimal scheduling sequence for all checkpoint handlings
so that the total completion time for all delivery routes is minimized.
